== Ensure AppArmor is enabled in the bootloader configuration
No audit procedure in ComplianceAsCode.

discussion:
## Ensure AppArmor is enabled in the bootloader configuration

Configure AppArmor to be enabled at boot time and verify that it has not been
overwritten by the bootloader boot parameters.

Note: This recommendation is designed around the grub bootloader, if LILO or
another bootloader is in use in your environment, enact equivalent settings.

**Rationale:**

AppArmor must be enabled at boot time in your bootloader configuration to
ensure that the controls it provides are not overridden.

steps.name: Ensure AppArmor is enabled in the bootloader configuration
steps.shell:
# Remediation is applicable only in certain platforms
if [ ! -f /.dockerenv ] && [ ! -f /run/.containerenv ]; then

# Correct the form of default kernel command line in GRUB
if grep -q '^\s*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=.*apparmor=.*\"' '/etc/default/grub' ; then
    # modify the GRUB command-line if an apparmor= arg already exists
    sed -i "s/\(^\s*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=\".*\)apparmor=[^[:space:]]\+\(.*\"\)/\1apparmor=1\2/" '/etc/default/grub'
# Add to already existing parameters
elif grep -q '^\s*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=' '/etc/default/grub' ; then
    # no apparmor=arg is present, append it
    sed -i "s/\(^\s*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=\".*\)\"/\1 apparmor=1\"/" '/etc/default/grub'
# Add parameters line if completely missing
else
    echo "GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=\"apparmor=1\"" >> '/etc/default/grub'
fi
if grep -q '^\s*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT=.*apparmor=.*\"' '/etc/default/grub' ; then
    # modify the GRUB command-line if an apparmor= arg already exists
    sed -i "s/\(^\s*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT=\".*\)apparmor=[^[:space:]]\+\(.*\"\)/\1apparmor=1\2/" '/etc/default/grub'
# Add to already existing parameters
elif grep -q '^\s*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT=' '/etc/default/grub' ; then
    # no apparmor=arg is present, append it
    sed -i "s/\(^\s*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT=\".*\)\"/\1 apparmor=1\"/" '/etc/default/grub'
# Add parameters line if completely missing
else
    echo "GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT=\"apparmor=1\"" >> '/etc/default/grub'
fi
# Correct the form of default kernel command line in GRUB
if grep -q '^\s*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=.*security=.*\"' '/etc/default/grub' ; then
    # modify the GRUB command-line if an security= arg already exists
    sed -i "s/\(^\s*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=\".*\)security=[^[:space:]]\+\(.*\"\)/\1security=apparmor\2/" '/etc/default/grub'
# Add to already existing parameters
elif grep -q '^\s*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=' '/etc/default/grub' ; then
    # no security=arg is present, append it
    sed -i "s/\(^\s*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=\".*\)\"/\1 security=apparmor\"/" '/etc/default/grub'
# Add parameters line if completely missing
else
    echo "GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX=\"security=apparmor\"" >> '/etc/default/grub'
fi
if grep -q '^\s*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT=.*security=.*\"' '/etc/default/grub' ; then
    # modify the GRUB command-line if an security= arg already exists
    sed -i "s/\(^\s*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT=\".*\)security=[^[:space:]]\+\(.*\"\)/\1security=apparmor\2/" '/etc/default/grub'
# Add to already existing parameters
elif grep -q '^\s*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT=' '/etc/default/grub' ; then
    # no security=arg is present, append it
    sed -i "s/\(^\s*GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT=\".*\)\"/\1 security=apparmor\"/" '/etc/default/grub'
# Add parameters line if completely missing
else
    echo "GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT=\"security=apparmor\"" >> '/etc/default/grub'
fi


update-grub

else
    >&2 echo 'Remediation is not applicable, nothing was done'
fi
